what: Step 2: Run a minimal nalanda workflow
title: Getting Started with Ellmer and Nalanda
text: ellmer works, nalanda::run_ai_on_chapters() uses setup returns structured outputs chapter simulations. also set package options beginning script need repeat arguments call.
code: library(nalanda)  options(   nalanda.integration = "vertexai",   nalanda.base_url = "https://ai-gateway.apps.cloud.rt.nyu.edu/v1/" )  demo_chapter <- "A short chapter about people from different groups cooperating."  res <- run_ai_on_chapters(   book_texts = demo_chapter,   groups = c("Democrat", "Republican"),   context_text = "You are simulating an American adult who politically identifies as a {identity}.",   question_text = "On a scale from 0 to 100, how warmly do you feel towards {group}s?",   n_simulations = 1,   temperature = 0,   model = "gemini-2.5-flash-lite" )  res ## # A tibble: 2 × 20 ##   chapter     sim identity party baseline_prompt post_prompt pre_rating_democrat post_rating_democrat pre_rating_republican ##   <chr>     <int> <chr>    <chr> <chr>           <chr>                     <int>                <int>                 <int> ## 1 chapter_1     1 Democrat Demo… You are simula… "You have …                  85                   85                    20 ## 2 chapter_1     1 Republi… Repu… You are simula… "You have …                  25                   40                    85 ## # ℹ 11 more variables: post_rating_republican <int>, pre_ingroup <int>, post_ingroup <int>, pre_outgroup <dbl>, ## #   post_outgroup <dbl>, pre_gap <dbl>, post_gap <dbl>, delta_ingroup <int>, delta_outgroup <dbl>, delta_gap <dbl>, ## #   chapter_excerpt <chr> # Inspect a real example output in a scrollable interactive table library(DT)  DT::datatable(   res,   rownames = FALSE,   filter = "top",   options = list(     scrollX = TRUE,     pageLength = 10,     autoWidth = TRUE   ) )

title: R Toolbox to answer the question: Do books really change lives?
text: nalanda package provides tools simulating, summarizing, plotting chapter-level AI reading responses. designed workflows ask whether books shift prosocial attitudes, outgroup warmth, affective polarization across chapters across whole books.

title: R Toolbox to answer the question: Do books really change lives?
text: can install development version nalanda GitHub :
code: install.packages(   'nalanda', repos = c(     'https://centerconflictcooperation.r-universe.dev',      'https://cloud.r-project.org'))

title: R Toolbox to answer the question: Do books really change lives?
text: main workflow three steps: run run_ai_on_chapters() get raw turn-level output convert raw turns chapter-level metrics compute_run_ai_metrics() summarize plot processed results README uses bundled toy data renders quickly require live API calls. Use processed chapter-level results directly time-series plotting helper: Synthetic chapter-level trajectories affective polarization change party. workflow scales : raw turn-level output run_ai_on_chapters() processing compute_run_ai_metrics() summary tables via summarize_chapter_scores() saved .rds simulation outputs book-level summaries via summarize_chapter_scores(..., aggregate_level = "book") visualization plot_chapter_trajectories(), plot_chapters_over_time(), plot_forest_books() API setup live minimal simulation example, see vignette:
code: library(nalanda)  raw_turns <- run_ai_on_chapters(   book_texts = "A short chapter about people from different groups cooperating.",   groups = c("Democrat", "Republican"),   context_text = "You are simulating an American adult who politically identifies as a {identity}.",   question_text = "On a scale from 0 to 100, how warmly do you feel towards {group}s?",   n_simulations = 2,   temperature = 0,   model = "gemini-2.5-flash-lite" )  chapter_results <- compute_run_ai_metrics(raw_turns) library(nalanda)  img_paths <- list(   Democrat = normalizePath("man/figures/dem.png"),   Republican = normalizePath("man/figures/rep.png") )  chapter_results <- compute_run_ai_metrics(toy_run_ai_turns)  head(chapter_results[, c("book", "chapter", "sim", "party", "delta_gap")]) #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>   book           chapter     sim party      delta_gap #>   <chr>          <chr>     <int> <chr>          <dbl> #> 1 Bridge Stories chapter_1     1 Democrat         3   #> 2 Common Ground  chapter_1     1 Democrat         4   #> 3 Bridge Stories chapter_1     1 Republican      11   #> 4 Common Ground  chapter_1     1 Republican       5   #> 5 Bridge Stories chapter_1     2 Democrat         3.5 #> 6 Common Ground  chapter_1     2 Democrat         4.5 plot_chapters_over_time(   chapters = chapter_results,   dv = "delta_gap",   group = "party",   y_label = "Affective Polarization (Delta Gap)",   plot_subtitle = "Bundled toy data: 2 simulations per party",   plot_title = "Results of 4 simulations per book per chapter",   error_bars = FALSE,   reverse_score = TRUE,   groups.order = "none",   facet = "book",   facets.order = "decreasing",   line_width = 1.2,   point_images = img_paths,   image_size = 0.09 ) vignette("getting-started", package = "nalanda")
